alt: NYC DOT cross-section diagram of Grand Street showing the proposed layout: two car travel lanes and a parking lane taking 23 feet, with only an 8-foot two-way bike lane squeezed into the remainder
credit: NYC Department of Transportation / Streetsblog NYC
story: New York City's DOT revealed plans for a two-way 'protected' bike lane on Grand Street in Lower Manhattan that is only 8 feet total — 4 feet per direction — less than half the recommended minimum width, while 23 of the street's 34 feet remain allocated to cars including space for double-parking.
why_funny: The city's own planning diagram shows cyclists getting a strip barely wider than a car door while the double-parking lane stays, then called it a 'protected' bike path.
